sections.content:
16,680 people

were counted on the census as "IT network professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.
IT network professionals design, set up and maintain computer networks, support the network users and fix problems which arise.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "IT network professionals" there were more men than women (92.3% compared with 7.7%).

This means "IT network professionals" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 92.3% and women made up 7.7% of "IT network professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "IT network professionals" included:

  • marine and waterways transport operatives
  • forestry and related workers
  • skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades supervisors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 35 to 39 years. Of the whole working population 11.5% were aged 35 to 39 years. For people working as "IT network professionals", 15.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "IT network professionals" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "IT network professionals" included:

  • cyber security professionals
  • customer service managers
  • secondary education teaching professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "IT network professionals", 7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (95.7% compared with 4.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (94.2%) than self-employed (5.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
